notes: Read the entire sole target unit. Preserve the distinction between historical organizing, characterizations of capitalist development, and convention commitments. Render the race-to-the-bottom metaphor as competition to lower labor standards; do not turn internal list letters into evidence IDs.

claims.claim_text: Since 2001, DSA's national political work has focused on opposing global capitalist development based on competitive reductions in labor standards.
Global capitalist development based on competitive reductions in labor standards has reduced working people's quality of life, including in the United States.
DSA has helped build community participation in citizen-labor alliances opposing the low-wage economy at national and local levels.
Community participation in citizen-labor alliances counters the conservative claim that organized labor's efforts are self-interested.
DSA's public political education presents competition to reduce labor standards as a systemic feature of global capitalist development rather than the conduct of one corporation.
DSA characterizes the global capitalist development model associated with competitive reductions in labor standards as irrational.
DSA has highlighted local, national and transnational efforts to develop alternatives based on fair trade, global labor and human rights, and equitable development.
Commitment to continue and deepen DSA's coordinated Low Wage Justice campaign, initiated at its 2001 convention.
Commitment to retain Wal-Mart as an example of corporate strategies that competitively reduce labor standards.
Commitment for DSA's NPC and national office to continue providing resources and information for local living-wage campaigns, immigrant-justice activism and labor support.
